children.text: The home of the Philippines' most celebrated mangoes, just a
15-minute
bangka ride from Iloilo. With mango farms and mango pizza, a Trappist monastery, and island hopping around small islets on the south coast, you can leisurely explore the whole island in a day or two.

Guimaras is an island of about 600 km² floating in the Guimaras Strait between Panay and Negros, and a small province where the whole island forms a single provincial unit. Long part of Iloilo province, it became a separate province in
and is made up of five municipalities: Jordan (the capital), Buenavista, Nueva Valencia, San Lorenzo, and Sibunag. It's only
15 minutes
by sea from Parola wharf in Iloilo City, yet the moment you set foot on the island, city noise gives way to a quiet countryside dotted with mango trees.

What put Guimaras on the map nationwide is its mangoes. Among the Philippines' carabao mangoes, those grown in Guimaras are famous for their high sweetness and rich aroma, and the island is home to the National Mango Research and Development Center. Mangoes are prized here to the point that bringing outside mangoes onto the island is banned, in order to protect the island's mango quality and keep it free of pests and disease. Every
May
, the Manggahan Festival celebrates the mango harvest.

The southwestern coast of the island, around Nueva Valencia, has its own charm. Around Alubihod Beach, small uninhabited islets and limestone rock formations are scattered offshore, and the Taklong Island National Marine Reserve is a well-preserved ecological area of mangroves and coral reefs. Attractions are scattered across the island, including Guisi Beach with its Spanish-era lighthouse ruins, the hilltop pilgrimage site of Balaan Bukid, and the Trappist monastery where monks make mango jam.

Guimaras suits travelers who'd rather enjoy a quiet island village, fresh fruit, and simple beaches than big resorts or flashy activities. It's a nice day trip from Iloilo, and equally good for an unhurried overnight stay at a beach resort.
In
July

2025, Republic Act No. 12225 upgraded the Taklong Island National Marine Reserve to the "Taklong–Tandog Islands Natural Park." Together, Taklong Island, Tandog Island, and 37 small islets cover about 1,143 hectares, protecting coral reefs, mangroves, and seagrass beds, and the area was proclaimed a marine reserve by President Corazon Aquino in
. In
, an oil spill from a sunken tanker badly damaged the mangrove forest, but it recovered through a restoration project and is now an ecotourism spot on the island's southwestern coast.

blocks.title: Eat mangoes and visit a mango farm

children.text: In season (roughly
March–May
), you can buy freshly picked mangoes cheaply from roadside stalls and markets. Walk among the mango trees around a farm or near the research center.
Mango pizza, sold at restaurants around Jordan, is a local specialty — a sweet-and-savory pie topped with cashews and mango, best enjoyed with a mango shake.

Our Lady of the Philippines Trappist Monastery, in San Miguel, Jordan, is memorable for its peaceful grounds and simple chapel. The monastery gift shop sells mango jam, mango cookies, and cashew products.
Rent a bangka at Alubihod Beach in Nueva Valencia to visit Ave Maria Island, small caves and rock islets, and snorkeling spots. A boat costs around

A protected area combining mangrove forest, seagrass beds, and coral reefs, known for its striking scenery of limestone rock islands cloaked in green forest. Entry and activities follow the reserve's management rules.

blocks.title: Guisi Lighthouse ruins and Guisi Beach

children.text: The ruins of a lighthouse (Faro de Punta Luzaran) that the Spanish government built in

at Guisi Point in Barangay Dolores, Nueva Valencia, remain today, and it is known as the second-oldest lighthouse in the Philippines. A new solar-powered lighthouse stands inside the rusty old tower, and the entrance fee is about
. Guisi Beach below the point is quiet and good for swimming.
A holy site on a hill about

above sea level in Barangay Balcon Melisa, Jordan, with a giant cross and a small chapel, and the cross can be seen even from the Iloilo coast. On Good Friday, a procession for the passion play "Pagtaltal sa Balaan Bukid," which starts from downtown Jordan, climbs the hill along the 14 Stations of the Cross, a path of about
1.7 km
. From the summit you can look down on the Iloilo Strait.
A three-story mansion built in

on a rock on the Buenavista coast, it was the summer house of Iloilo's prominent Lopez family and has been designated a heritage house by the National Historical Institute. The interior is private property, so you mainly admire the exterior and the coastal scenery, and the entrance fee is about

The beaches and island hopping around Nueva Valencia in the south take about
1 hour

one way from Jordan, so if you want to reach the beach on a day trip, it's better to visit just one monastery and head straight south. On rainy days or when the sea is rough, the northern land route above is enough on its own.

items.subtitle: Holy Week, centered on Balaan Bukid

children.text: Take the earliest boat from Parola wharf in Iloilo across to Jordan.
Watch the passion play procession begin in downtown Jordan.
Walk the 14 Stations of the Cross (about
1.7 km
) up to the cross and chapel at the summit of Balaan Bukid.
Come down before sunset and take a bangka to Parola before the return boats get crowded.

Good Friday draws huge crowds — as many as about 30,000 visitors were expected even in 2023. Event times and traffic controls change every year, so check announcements from the Guimaras provincial government and the diocese.
It's about
1 hour 10 minutes
from Manila to Iloilo International Airport (ILO). From the airport to Parola wharf downtown takes about
45 minutes–1 hour
by taxi or Grab.
There are also daily direct flights to Iloilo from Cebu's Mactan Airport, with a flight time of about
1 hour

Direct flights between Manila and Iloilo are operated by Cebu Pacific, Philippine Airlines (PAL), PAL Express, and AirAsia Philippines. Fares vary greatly by season, so the earlier you book, the better.
Iloilo International Airport is in Cabatuan, about
20 km
from the city. Regular Grab cars generally cost
, and fares rise during busy hours.
Motor bangkas run from Parola wharf in Iloilo City to Jordan wharf about every
15 minutes
(every
30 minutes–1 hour
at quiet times), and the fare is
per person (
after

7–9 PM
, so check at the wharf.
There is also a route toward Buenavista, and if you want to bring a vehicle across, take a RoRo ferry to Jordan from Iloilo's RoRo terminal.
Bangka fares and schedules can change based on decisions by shipping authorities and the provincial government, so check the latest notice.

There are also small bangkas that cross directly from Negros Island between Pulupandan in Negros Occidental and the eastern Guimaras wharf, but they run infrequently and are sensitive to waves, so most people come via Iloilo.
Wharf and boat information is available on the Guimaras provincial government's
official website
In Iloilo, take a bangka to Jordan from Parola wharf or Ortiz wharf.
Coming from Bacolod, take a fast craft to Iloilo first (about
1 hour
), then head to Parola wharf.
Fast crafts between Bacolod and Iloilo are run by Weesam Express, with one-way fares listed at about
depending on class. There are around four sailings a day and cancellations are frequent in the rainy season, so check the latest schedule and fares.

On the island, tricycles or multicabs (small truck-based jeepneys) are the way to get around. You can charter a fixed-rate tricycle for an island loop at the tourist information center by Jordan wharf, costing about
a day depending on the route.
A shared jeepney or multicab from Jordan to Nueva Valencia costs about
per person and takes about
1 hour
An island-loop tricycle on a route that takes about 8 hours is listed at around
per tricycle (up to 5 people). Places outside the route, such as the wind farm, cost extra.
Motorbike rental costs about
per day; always check the license and helmet before renting.
The dry season, from
December
to
May
, is best for touring the island and enjoying the beaches. In particular, from
March
to
May
is the peak of the mango harvest, when you can eat the best mangoes at the lowest prices. Around the provincial founding anniversary in
late May
, the Manggahan Festival brings a mango-eating contest, a parade, and an agricultural fair.
From
June
to
November
is the rainy season, and afternoon showers and the southwest monsoon can lead to canceled hopping tours in the southern waters some days. Typhoons mainly affect the area from
August–November
, and bangka service between Iloilo and Guimaras can be suspended during these. Visitor numbers rise sharply during Holy Week before Easter, for the Balaan Bukid pilgrimage and passion play.
The
Manggahan Festival was held
mid-May to May 24

to mark the province's 34th founding anniversary (an official announcement says it started on the 15th, while a news report says the 17th). The highlight, all-you-can-eat mango tasting, was run so that each person got
30 minutes
for
, and on weekends it continued until
. The province's founding anniversary is
(the day it was upgraded to an independent province); schedules and prices change every year, so check the provincial government's latest notice before you visit.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions.
Guimaras accommodation is concentrated mostly around Alubihod Beach in Nueva Valencia. Beachfront bungalows and small to mid-size resorts run about

a night, and weekends in peak season get crowded with day-trippers and overnight visitors from Iloilo, so book ahead. There are also small hotels and guesthouses near Jordan, the provincial capital, which you can choose based on how you plan your island loop.

Mangoes are, without question, the star of the food here. You can try nearly every dish made with mango — fresh mango, mango shakes, mango pizza, mango ketchup, mango jam, and dried mango. Beach resorts and coastal restaurants serve grilled fish, squid, and shellfish dishes at reasonable prices. Mango jam and cookies from the Trappist monastery gift shop, and dried mango from the souvenir shops in front of Jordan wharf, make popular gifts.

The Pitstop Restaurant in downtown Jordan is the best-known restaurant for mango pizza and also serves adapted dishes such as beef bone soup with mango. On the Alubihod Beach side, mid-range lodgings such as Raymen Beach Resort, which takes bookings for both bungalow-style rooms and hopping boats, are widely known. The Trappist monastery also has a guesthouse for people who come for a retreat or meditation, and if you only look around without staying, no reservation is needed.
When you arrive at Jordan wharf, check the island map and the fixed tricycle rates at the tourist information center first — it leads to fewer disputes than negotiating individually with touts.
The island loop covers quite a distance. If you're only visiting for the day, it's best to focus on either the north (monastery, pilgrimage site, mangoes) or the south (beaches, hopping).
ATMs are only found in a few places, such as Jordan, so bring enough cash from Iloilo.
Mangoes cost much more and taste less good outside the harvest season. A visit in
March–May
is recommended.
Taking mango souvenirs back to Iloilo is fine, but check quarantine rules for air travel and for taking them abroad. Bringing fresh mangoes into Korea is generally not allowed.
Check the time of the last bangka; it's safest to head back toward Jordan by around
Alubihod Beach gets shallow at low tide. Plan your swimming and hopping around the tide schedule.
Entry to the Trappist monastery is free, and the monastery and gift shop close at
, so visit in the morning or early afternoon. It is a sacred place, so dress modestly.

Taklong Island Natural Park is said to limit the number of visitors at one time to about 30, so ask in advance through a tour operator or an Alubihod resort. On arrival, register and make a small donation.
Many places charge only small entrance fees, such as
for Roca Encantada and
for the Guisi lighthouse, so bring plenty of small bills.
Guimaras was made a special quarantine zone by Proclamation No. 314 in
, so bringing mango fruit, seeds, or saplings from outside the island is prohibited. Baggage is inspected at the wharf, and anything found is confiscated and destroyed at the carrier's expense.
Bringing mangoes or mango saplings bought outside Guimaras onto the island is prohibited. They will be confiscated if found during quarantine checks at the wharf.
Collecting coral or shells, fishing, and touching marine life are banned in the marine reserve. Follow the guidance of the reserve staff.
Bangka service is suspended when waves run high. During the rainy season, build extra time into your schedule and always wear a life jacket.
Rural roads have very little lighting at night. Avoid renting a motorbike for nighttime driving.
Entrance fees and environmental charges at well-known attractions vary by municipality and change from time to time, so check the latest notice.
There are warning signs that the old tower of the Guisi lighthouse is badly rusted and that the path up has no railings. If you're with children, it's safer not to climb.
On Good Friday, pilgrims flood in, so boats get crowded and accommodations fill up early; plan ahead and leave plenty of time for the return trip.
